findings.title: Team administrators are rejected by an ANDed role check
findings.body: The authorization check requires the caller to satisfy both `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`. Team membership roles are distinct, so an administrator who is not the booking's organizer fails this condition and receives FORBIDDEN, despite the product UI treating team admins or owners as eligible (`isUserTeamAdminOrOwner`). Use an OR check so either role can manage a team booking.

findings.title: The guest list has no server-side size limit
findings.body: Any authenticated attendee is authorized to call this endpoint, and `guests` is an unbounded array. A caller can submit thousands of arbitrary valid addresses in one request, creating corresponding attendee records, calendar invitations, and emails; repeated calls also notify every existing attendee. This makes the endpoint an email-spam and resource-exhaustion primitive. Enforce a reasonable maximum number of guests server-side (and ideally a per-booking/event-type guest policy).

findings.title: Attendees are persisted before calendar synchronization succeeds
findings.body: The handler writes the new attendees to the booking before calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`. If the calendar update fails (for example, because an attendee/admin actor lacks the organizer's calendar credentials), the mutation rejects but the database still shows the guests as added, while the external calendar and notification flow were not updated. This leaves booking state inconsistent and retries can behave differently. The operation needs compensation/outbox handling or a deliberate failure strategy that does not leave the completed database mutation presented as a failed add.

findings.title: Guest and blacklist comparisons are case-sensitive
findings.body: Email addresses are compared directly against stored attendees and the lowercased blacklist, but input guest addresses are never normalized. A request using a different case can bypass `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` and can add a second logical copy of an existing attendee (or trigger a database uniqueness failure, depending on collation/constraints). Normalize and compare email addresses case-insensitively before filtering, persistence, and deciding which recipients are new.

findings.title: The endpoint permits adding guests to cancelled or rejected bookings
findings.body: Authorization is the only booking-state validation; a direct API caller who was an attendee, organizer, or team manager can add guests to a cancelled or rejected booking. The handler then creates attendee records and sends confirmed calendar/email updates for an event that will not occur. Restrict this mutation to the supported active booking statuses (and any applicable time/recurrence rules) on the server rather than relying on the dashboard action visibility.
